q: A _____ battery is one kind of galvanic cell, a device that can change chemical energy to electrical energy.
e: A car battery is one kind of galvanic cell, a device that can change chemical energy to electrical energy. A car battery is a secondary cell: it can both supply electrical energy and be recharged. Car is the word this version is asking about.

q: In a chemical cell with zinc and copper plates, _____, the more electropositive of the two metals, ionises by loss of electrons.
e: In a chemical cell with zinc and copper plates, Zinc, the more electropositive of the two metals, ionises by loss of electrons. Ionisation in solution or in the melt produces mobile ions that can carry current.

q: In a chemical cell with zinc and copper plates, electrons pass from zinc to copper through the _____.
e: In a chemical cell with zinc and copper plates, electrons pass from zinc to copper through the wire. Copper plates, electrons pass from zinc to copper through the wire.

q: The reaction at the zinc electrode in a chemical cell is $Zn(s) \rightarrow Zn^{2+}(aq) +$ _____.
e: The reaction at the zinc electrode in a chemical cell is Zn(s) to Zn^2+(aq) + 2e^-. Electrodes are the conductors where oxidation and reduction happen during electrolysis.

q: At the copper surface in a chemical cell, hydrogen ions from the dilute sulphuric acid are _____ and hydrogen gas is liberated.
e: At the copper surface in a chemical cell, hydrogen ions from the dilute sulphuric acid are reduced and hydrogen gas is liberated. Concentrated sulphuric acid is a strong acid, a dehydrating agent and an oxidising agent.

q: The phenomenon where bubbles of hydrogen adhere to the surface of the copper electrode, cutting off contact with the electrolyte, is called _____.
e: The phenomenon where bubbles of hydrogen adhere to the surface of the copper electrode, cutting off contact with the electrolyte, is called polarisation. An electrolyte ionises in solution or in the molten state so the ions can carry current. Electrodes are the conductors where oxidation and reduction happen during electrolysis.

q: Polarisation _____ down the reaction at the electrode.
e: Polarisation slows down the reaction at the electrode. Electrodes are the conductors where oxidation and reduction happen during electrolysis.

q: The two metals used to convert chemical energy into electrical energy must be _____ separated in the electrochemical series.
e: The two metals used to convert chemical energy into electrical energy must be widely separated in the electrochemical series. The two metals in a cell must sit far enough apart in the electrochemical series to give a useful voltage.

q: The greater the difference in reactivity between the two metals, the greater the _____ or electromotive force (emf) of the cell is observed.
e: The greater the difference in reactivity between the two metals, the greater the voltage or electromotive force (emf) of the cell is observed. The greater the voltage or electromotive force (emf) of the cell is observed. Voltage is the word this version is asking about.

q: Electromotive force (emf) is the maximum potential difference between two electrodes of a galvanic or voltaic cell and it is measured in _____.
e: Electromotive force (emf) is the maximum potential difference between two electrodes of a galvanic or voltaic cell and it is measured in volt (V). Electrodes are the conductors where oxidation and reduction happen during electrolysis. Volt (V) is the word this version is asking about.
